faq.q: What is the most valuable commodity in life?
faq.a: For most people, it’s time and attention. Time is finite and can’t be earned back, and attention decides how well that time is actually lived.

faq.q: Why is time more valuable than money?
faq.a: Money can be lost and earned again, but time can’t be stored, replaced, or borrowed. Much of what we spend money on is really an attempt to buy back time.
It’s the idea that when information is abundant, human attention becomes scarce, so apps, media, and advertisers compete to capture and hold it.

faq.q: How can I protect my time without becoming rigid?
faq.a: Start with a short list of priorities, protect one daily block for them, and leave margin in your schedule. The goal is choosing on purpose, not filling every minute.

faq.q: How do I know if I’m wasting my time?
faq.a: Common signs include ending the week unable to name anything you did on purpose, feeling tired but unsatisfied, and repeatedly postponing what you say matters most.

faq.q: Is rest a waste of my most valuable commodity?
faq.a: No. Rest, play, and unhurried time with people are some of the best uses of your time. Protecting time is about intention, not constant productivity.
